title: CreativityPrism task registry entry
description: Contract consumed by runner/run.py and runner/artifacts.py. Exists mainly so editors stop guessing; schemastore maps **/tasks/*.yaml to the Ansible tasks schema, which these files are not.

name.description: Registry key. Must match the file name and the --task argument.

domain.description: Grouping label for reporting only; not consumed by the runner.

folder.description: Repo-relative path to the task bundle.

adapter.description: Repo-relative path to the adapter script.

environment.description: Short env name; the runner pre-flights creativityprism-<environment>. 'modern' and 'legacy' ship with the repo; a contributor may name their own and add registry/environments/<name>.yml. Defaults to modern.

limit_supported.description: Whether the task can honour --limit. Absent means false, and the runner rejects --limit.

slurm.description: Per-task SBATCH directive overrides for --slurm. Keys are directive names without the leading dashes; underscores are accepted for dashes (cpus_per_task -> cpus-per-task). A null or empty value drops the directive. These override runner/slurm_template.sbatch and are themselves overridden by --slurm-override. Values are cluster-specific, so partition and account names must be set for the cluster in use.

uses_judge.description: Whether evaluation calls an LLM judge. False means --judge-model is a documented no-op for this task (scoring is execution, embedding distance, an n-gram index, ...). Consumed by the gates and by RUNNING_GUIDE Track C; absent means false.

loader_parser.description: How result_analysis/loader.py turns this task's artifacts into rows: '<module>:<callable>'. The callable takes (inference, evaluation) as [(stem, data), ...] pairs and returns row dicts. Absent means the task's results stay out of the shared table.

stages.description: Which stages this task has. Defaults to both. A generation-only task that is scored by hand later declares ['inference'] and is then not expected -- by the gates or by the runner -- to produce an evaluation artifact.

distribution.description: How the task's data reaches users. 'bundled' (the default when absent): the Hub dataset ships it. 'fetch': upstream carries no license, so the Hub dataset ships item ids and source references with the text null, and release/scripts/fetch_upstream.py pulls the text from `upstream`. Flipping to 'bundled' is the whole change when upstream adds a license.

upstream.description: Where the task's data comes from: who published it, under what licence, and what we changed. A task with distribution: fetch must also pin `commit` and list `files`.

license.description: SPDX id where there is one; 'none' when the upstream carries no licence.

commit.description: Full commit sha. A branch name would let upstream change the data under us.

ours.description: Our data file, relative to the task bundle's data/processed/.

theirs.description: Upstream file, relative to the upstream repo root.

field.description: Key read from each upstream row.

into.description: Dotted path in our row that receives prefix + the upstream value.

paper.description: Link to the paper the data was published with.

modifications.description: What we changed, in one sentence or two. CC-BY and Apache-2.0 upstreams require this to be stated.
